title: Stalks of $\mathcal J\mathcal F$, of $\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F$ and of powers of an ideal sheaf
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a sheaf of ideals (a sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module of $\mathcal O_X$) and $\mathcal F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\mathcal J\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal F$ be the image of the multiplication map $\mathcal J\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$, $a\otimes s\mapsto as$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F$ the cokernel of the inclusion $\mathcal J\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$, and $\mathcal J^1=\mathcal J$, $\mathcal J^{n+1}=\mathcal J\cdot\mathcal J^n$ (the product just defined, with $\mathcal F=\mathcal J^n$, a sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module of $\mathcal O_X$). Let $x\in X$, with stalks and germs as in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Then: (1) the stalk map $\mathcal J_x\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ of the inclusion is injective, so $\mathcal J_x$ is identified with an ideal of the ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$; likewise $(\mathcal J\mathcal F)_x\to\mathcal F_x$ is injective; (2) under this identification $(\mathcal J\mathcal F)_x=\mathcal J_x\mathcal F_x$, the $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-submodule of $\mathcal F_x$ generated by the products $a\,m$, $a\in\mathcal J_x$, $m\in\mathcal F_x$; (3) the stalk at $x$ of the quotient map $\mathcal F\to\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F$ induces an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules $\mathcal F_x/\mathcal J_x\mathcal F_x\cong(\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F)_x$; (4) for every $n\ge1$, $(\mathcal J^n)_x=(\mathcal J_x)^n$ as ideals of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $(\mathcal J^n\mathcal F)_x=(\mathcal J_x)^n\mathcal F_x$ as submodules of $\mathcal F_x$, and $(\mathcal F/\mathcal J^n\mathcal F)_x\cong\mathcal F_x/(\mathcal J_x)^n\mathcal F_x$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01AG (lemma-abelian: a complex of O_X-modules is exact iff it is exact on all stalks; kernels, images and cokernels are computed stalkwise) and Lemma 01CB (lemma-stalk-tensor-product: (F tensor G)_x = F_x tensor G_x); the statement combines them and is used without proof in Stacks, Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0CYV (coherent.tex, lemma-systems-with-proper-support)

proof.text: *Clause (1).* Write $i:\mathcal J\to\mathcal O_X$ for the inclusion; it is $\mathcal O_X$-linear and $i_U:\mathcal J(U)\to\mathcal O_X(U)$ is the inclusion of a submodule for every open $U$, compatibly with restrictions. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] (1) the $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear map $i_x:\mathcal J_x\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is injective (directly: if $a\in\mathcal J(U)$ has $i_x(a_x)=(a)_x=0$ in $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, then $a|_W=0$ in $\mathcal O_X(W)$ for some open $x\in W\subseteq U$, hence in $\mathcal J(W)$, so $a_x=0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]). Its image is an $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-submodule of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, i.e. an ideal, which we identify with $\mathcal J_x$; under this identification $a_x\in\mathcal J_x$ is the germ of $a$ as a section of $\mathcal O_X$, and $\mathcal J_x$ acts on any $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module through $\mathcal J_x\subseteq\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Likewise $\mathcal J\mathcal F=\operatorname{Im}(\mu)$, $\mu:\mathcal J\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ the multiplication map, is by definition the kernel of the cokernel map of $\mu$, a kernel in $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$, hence a sectionwise sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module of $\mathcal F$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; so the same argument ([lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] (1), or (4)) shows that $(\mathcal J\mathcal F)_x\to\mathcal F_x$ is injective.

source.place: Modules, Section 17.3 (kernels, lines 102-115) and Lemma 01AG (lemma-abelian, line 149)

proof.text: *The multiplication map on stalks.* The presheaf maps $\mathcal J(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X(U)}\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal F(U)$, $a\otimes s\mapsto as$, are $\mathcal O_X(U)$-linear and commute with restrictions ($(as)|_V=a|_Vs|_V$), so by the universal property of sheafification of presheaves of modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] they induce the unique $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\mu:\mathcal J\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ with $\mu_U(a\otimes s)=as$, where $a\otimes s$ denotes the image in $(\mathcal J\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F)(U)$ under the sheafification map [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-tensor] there is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules $\tau:(\mathcal J\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F)_x\cong\mathcal J_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\mathcal F_x$ with $\tau((a\otimes s)_x)=a_x\otimes s_x$. Hence $\mu_x\circ\tau^{-1}(a_x\otimes s_x)=\mu_x((a\otimes s)_x)=(\mu_U(a\otimes s))_x=(as)_x=a_x\,s_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Since every pair $(\alpha,m)\in\mathcal J_x\times\mathcal F_x$ is of the form $(a_x,s_x)$ with $a\in\mathcal J(U)$, $s\in\mathcal F(U)$ on one open $U\ni x$ (each is a germ, and the open neighbourhoods of $x$ are directed), $\mu_x\circ\tau^{-1}$ is the multiplication map $\mathcal J_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\mathcal F_x\to\mathcal F_x$, $\alpha\otimes m\mapsto\alpha m$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01AG (lemma-abelian, line 149) and Lemma 01CB (lemma-stalk-tensor-product, line 2333)

proof.text: *Clause (2).* By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] (4) applied to $\mu$, the stalk $(\mathcal J\mathcal F)_x=(\operatorname{Im}\mu)_x$, viewed inside $\mathcal F_x$ by clause (1), equals $\mu_x((\mathcal J\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F)_x)$, which by the previous step is the image of $\mathcal J_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\mathcal F_x\to\mathcal F_x$, $\alpha\otimes m\mapsto\alpha m$. Every element of the tensor product is a finite sum $\sum_k\alpha_k\otimes m_k$, so this image is the set of finite sums $\sum_k\alpha_km_k$ with $\alpha_k\in\mathcal J_x$, $m_k\in\mathcal F_x$; it is an $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-submodule ($r\alpha_km_k=(r\alpha_k)m_k$ with $r\alpha_k\in\mathcal J_x$, $\mathcal J_x$ being an ideal), hence the submodule $\mathcal J_x\mathcal F_x$ generated by the products.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01AG (lemma-abelian, line 149) and Lemma 01CB (lemma-stalk-tensor-product, line 2333)

proof.text: *Clause (3).* Let $k:\mathcal J\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ be the inclusion and $q:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F$ its cokernel. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] (3), $q_x:\mathcal F_x\to(\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F)_x$ is a surjective $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear map with kernel $k_x((\mathcal J\mathcal F)_x)$, which is $\mathcal J_x\mathcal F_x$ by clause (2). So $q_x$ induces an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules $\mathcal F_x/\mathcal J_x\mathcal F_x\cong(\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F)_x$ (first isomorphism theorem).

source.place: Modules, Section 17.3 (cokernels, lines 117-130: Coker(phi)_x = Coker(phi_x)) and Lemma 01AG

proof.text: *Clause (4), by induction on $n$.* First, every $\mathcal J^n$ is a sheaf of ideals: $\mathcal J^1=\mathcal J$, and $\mathcal J^{n+1}=\mathcal J\cdot\mathcal J^n$ is a sectionwise sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module of $\mathcal J^n$ (step 1), hence of $\mathcal O_X$; so clauses (1)-(3), proved for an arbitrary sheaf of ideals and an arbitrary $\mathcal O_X$-module, apply with $\mathcal J^n$ in place of $\mathcal J$. For $n=1$, $(\mathcal J^1)_x=\mathcal J_x=(\mathcal J_x)^1$. Suppose $(\mathcal J^n)_x=(\mathcal J_x)^n$ as ideals of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Clause (2) with $\mathcal F=\mathcal J^n$ gives $(\mathcal J^{n+1})_x=\mathcal J_x\cdot(\mathcal J^n)_x$ inside $(\mathcal J^n)_x$; the stalk of the inclusion $\mathcal J^n\to\mathcal O_X$ is injective and $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear (clause (1)), so it carries $\alpha\cdot m$ ($\alpha\in\mathcal J_x$, $m\in(\mathcal J^n)_x$) to the ring product $\alpha m$ in $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, and the stalk of the composite inclusion $\mathcal J^{n+1}\to\mathcal J^n\to\mathcal O_X$ maps $(\mathcal J^{n+1})_x$ onto the ideal generated by the products $\alpha m$, $\alpha\in\mathcal J_x$, $m\in(\mathcal J_x)^n$, that is $(\mathcal J_x)^{n+1}$. Finally, applying clauses (2) and (3) to the sheaf of ideals $\mathcal J^n$ and the module $\mathcal F$ gives $(\mathcal J^n\mathcal F)_x=(\mathcal J^n)_x\mathcal F_x=(\mathcal J_x)^n\mathcal F_x$ and $(\mathcal F/\mathcal J^n\mathcal F)_x\cong\mathcal F_x/(\mathcal J_x)^n\mathcal F_x$.

Proof written in five steps: (1) injectivity of stalks of sub-O_X-modules, J_x as an ideal; the multiplication map mu: J (x) F -> F and its stalk, identified via the existing 01CB node lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-tensor (unit sk-thm-reduction, used as a generic tool lemma) with alpha (x) m -> alpha m; (2) (JF)_x = image of mu_x = J_x F_x; (3) F_x/J_xF_x = (F/JF)_x from stalks of cokernels; (4) induction on n for J^n, applying (1)-(3) to the ideal sheaf J^n. Stalk exactness of O_X-modules (Stacks 01AG with the text before it) had no node: created lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact (unsplit; Mathlib has only the abelian-sheaf case, TopCat.Sheaf.exact_iff_stalkFunctor_map_exact, and SheafOfModules.toSheaf preserving finite limits, not cokernels).
